A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Chimera research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete supplementary material support comparison, including matching relocated displays and image-based extraction examples.

before.justification: v2 reports original Chimera results on reasoning and structural-extraction benchmarks, masking and expert-count ablations, and qualitative extraction examples.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds DPO post-training results, MME perception evaluation, attention analysis and router-error measurements.

M1.justification: v3 adds optional Direct Preference Optimization post-training to produce Chimera† (Sections 4.2 and 9). This extends training while retaining the original encoders, linear router, GSCM mechanism and two-stage alignment/instruction-tuning procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds MME perception evaluation, covering tasks such as object existence, counting, recognition and OCR. It also uses MathV-360K problems for DPO within the existing mathematical domain. The original training mixtures and reasoning/extraction benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: v3 Table 1 adds scored MathVista comparisons with InternVL-MPO-8B and Ovis1.6-Gemma2-9B. Existing comparator rows remain. Newly discussed GeoX, MoVA and MoME do not have corresponding scored comparisons establishing additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v3 adds one-epoch DPO training on 60K preference pairs and MME/router evaluation procedures. The reported intermediate sample for constructing Table-SE/Doc-SE changes from 1,100 to 6,000 pages. Final benchmark sizes remain 100 tables and 205 documents; the PDFs do not establish rerunning the retained evaluations.

E4.justification: v3 adds direct investigation of two central components: attention distributions with versus without GSCM and router confusion errors (Figure 4 and Table 7). These substantially extend the diagnostic evidence. Existing masking-ratio and expert-count ablations remain, as do the qualitative extraction examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests for Chimera's results. The 16 responses generated per DPO problem are preference-data construction, not repeated-run uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Original benchmark scores remain unchanged, including Chimera-8B's 64.9 on MathVista and 32.4 on MathVerse. v3 adds 68.3 for DPO-trained Chimera†, alongside InternVL-MPO's 67.3 and Ovis1.6-Gemma2's 67.2, plus MME results, 95.4% router accuracy and attention findings. The 68.3 result uses additional training rather than revising the original model's score.

T1.justification: The routing, feature-concatenation and cross-entropy equations are mathematically unchanged. Combining the expert-set displays and renumbering equations are presentation edits. v3 adds no theorem, proof or formal DPO derivation.

C1.justification: The central expert-integration, GSCM and reasoning/extraction claims remain. v3 adds the introductory claim that limited-data DPO further improves reasoning and promotes the existing lightweight router into the explicit contribution list.

C2.justification: v3 attributes router errors to dataset-level domain labels and mixed-domain general images, suggesting image-level annotation as a remedy. It also interprets MME results as indicating minimal general-capability degradation. Existing explanations concerning excessive masking and overly specialized experts are retained.

D1.justification: v3 documents sampling 10K MathV-360K problems, generating 16 responses each, and filtering preference pairs through rule-based correctness matching. It identifies the CFFF computing platform and states that training datasets are public. The project homepage link is removed, while a future weights/data-release promise remains.

R1.justification: v3 adds ten references and a targeted comparison with MoVA's multi-turn expert calling and MoME's soft-weighted encoder fusion in Section 13. The broad generalist-versus-specialist positioning remains. The earlier connection between benchmark construction and OmniDocBench's approach is omitted.

P1.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes existing content: expert-selection discussion and masking ablations move to supplements, supplementary sections are restructured, and references move after them. Variant names become Chimera throughout, with abstract, introduction and author/affiliation edits. Some cross-references become stale, including the unresolved 'Fig. ??' in Section 15.2.

P2.justification: v3 adds an attention heatmap and router/MME tables, expands MathVista's table with a preference-optimization block, and relocates existing dataset, expert-task and masking displays into supplements. Captions and expert markers are revised. The core diagrams, document-category radar plot and extraction examples are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens support for the framework through attention/router diagnostics and general-perception testing, while documenting a DPO extension and clarifying nearby expert-mixture work. These are useful additions beyond the retained original results. The gain is limited by an overbroad general-performance-preservation interpretation despite Table 10's 30-point OCR deficits relative to InternVL2 at both sizes, and by newly broken cross-references.
